rawOutput.title: Use the Product Rule Independently
rawOutput.rationale: This is a conceptual and problem-solving sequence for learning the product rule from scratch. Four short sessions fit the available 15-minute windows. The sequence begins with one complete example shown step by step, moves to guided use, then fades support through retrieval and independent application.

sessions.title: Understand the Product Rule
sessions.objective: Build a clear model of when and why the product rule is used.
sessions.amountLabel: Product rule formula and one complete worked example
contentTargets: Recognizing a product of two differentiable functions
Interpreting and applying (fg)' = f'g + fg'
completionEvidence: Explain what each term in the product rule represents
Apply the rule alongside a complete example to differentiate one product

sessions.title: Use the Procedure with Guidance
sessions.objective: Apply the product rule one visible step at a time to products of power functions.
contentTargets: Separating a product into f and g
Differentiating each factor and assembling the result
completionEvidence: Construct the four required parts: f, g, f', and g'
Solve two product-rule problems with step prompts

sessions.title: Retrieve and Apply the Rule
sessions.objective: Recall the product rule and use it with reduced support.
sessions.amountLabel: Rule recall and two reduced-support problems
contentTargets: Retrieving the product rule from memory
Applying the rule without a displayed template
completionEvidence: Recall the product rule without notes
Solve two product-rule derivatives and correct any assembly errors

sessions.title: Demonstrate Independent Use
sessions.objective: Choose and execute the product rule independently in mixed examples.
contentTargets: Distinguishing products from expressions that do not require the product rule
Completing and checking product-rule derivatives independently
completionEvidence: Classify three expressions by whether they require the product rule
Solve the applicable derivatives independently and verify each result

activities.correctAnswer: It is used when the function is a product of two differentiable functions.

activities.feedback: The repaired answer should name the product and the differentiable functions. If your first answer was too broad, narrow it to products only.

activities.body: Give the idea again in one or two sentences.

activities.correctAnswer: You use the product rule when you are differentiating a product of two differentiable functions.
activities.feedback: This final explanation should be clear, brief, and accurate. It should show that you can recognize the situation without naming extra formulas.
